title: ODRS Offer
description: A supplier's bound response to a specific data request: 'here is what I can deliver against your spec, at this price, by this date, with these deviations.' An offer references a REQUEST (required) and optionally the supplier's standing CAPABILITY. The deviations block is the heart of the object: real offers rarely match a spec exactly, and unstated deviations are how deliveries fail.

request.description: The data request this offer answers. REQUIRED — an offer without a request is a capability, and ODRS has a separate object for that.

capability.description: The supplier's standing capability this offer draws on, if published.

quantity.description: What the supplier commits to deliver. May be less than the request's full quantity — partial offers are first-class (requests declare data.quantity.minimum for exactly this reason).

sample.description: Proposed sample terms. SHOULD mirror or improve on the request's acceptance.sample.

pricing.description: The quoted price. Optional (an offer without pricing is an expression of serious interest pending negotiation), but when present the basis rule applies exactly as in requests.

amount.description: Exact quote. Use either amount, or min+max, not both.

deadline.description: When the offered quantity would be fully delivered.

licensing_granted.description: Rights the supplier grants under this offer. Same flags as request.licensing; the buyer diffs this against their requirement.

deviations.description: Explicit differences from the request's specification. THE most important block in an offer: 'we can deliver everything except 10ms sync — we achieve 15ms' stated up front is a negotiation; discovered at delivery it is a dispute. Each deviation names the request field it deviates from.

path.description: Dotted path into the request document, e.g. 'capture.synchronization.maximum_error_ms' or 'diversity.distinct_environments.minimum'.

requested.description: The request's value, for the reader's convenience.

proposed.description: What the supplier proposes instead. REQUIRED.

note.description: Why, and what it means for the buyer.

expires_at.description: After this instant the offer lapses without action by either party.

status.description: Offer lifecycle. Acceptance in ODRS is a status signal, not a contract — the parties' agreement governs.
